subject.title: fix(codex): cap compaction override warning cache via createDedupeCache

question: Should the Codex ignored-compaction-override warning state use a 4096-entry LRU despite the related maintainer policy against arbitrary warning-cache caps without measured owner-path growth?
rationale: The patch is mechanically correct and this key can vary with agent IDs, but choosing an eviction threshold and allowing old diagnostics to reappear is an owner-level lifecycle decision that tests and source inspection cannot settle.

options.title: Require Codex lifecycle evidence
options.body: Keep the PR open until the owner provides measured growth or a concrete key-space analysis and explains why 4096-entry LRU eviction is the canonical boundary.

options.title: Accept bounded re-warning
options.body: Merge the current mitigation and explicitly accept that old ignored-override combinations may warn again after eviction.

options.title: Reject defensive cap
options.body: Close the PR under the sibling policy and revisit only with an observed resource failure or lifecycle-owned cleanup design.

recommendation.title: Require Codex lifecycle evidence
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open until the owner provides measured growth or a concrete key-space analysis and explains why 4096-entry LRU eviction is the canonical boundary.
